adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts, the code wraps the refresh token fetch in refreshOAuthTokens(). According to refreshOAuthTokens.ts, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, it calls the external endpoint instead of the refreshFunction. The parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts shows that when credential sharing is enabled, it uses minimumTokenResponseSchema which only validates access_token and a number (expiry). However, the Webex VideoApiAdapter at line 88+ processes responseBody expecting the full Webex token response structure (access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, refresh_token_expires_in, token_type). The finding correctly identifies that when using the shared endpoint, the response won't contain all the fields Webex code expects, potentially causing issues. However, looking more carefully at the code flow - handleWebexResponse is called on the response, and the Webex adapter doesn't use parseRefreshTokenResponse directly. The refreshOAuthTokens just returns the fetch response, which then goes through handleWebexResponse. So the actual token parsing happens after. The issue is that the shared endpoint returns a minimal response that may not have refresh_token, but the Webex code expects it. This is a valid concern about compatibility.
